Stokes flow with Taylor-Hood elements

Source: R/stokes.R
stokes_problem.Rd

stokes_problem() defines the incompressible Stokes equations

Usage

stokes_problem(mesh, viscosity = 1, body_force = c(0, 0), bcs = list())

velocity_bc(value = c(0, 0), marker = "boundary", components = c("x", "y"))

Arguments

mesh

A pde_mesh().

viscosity

Kinematic viscosity nu > 0 (number or function(x, y)).

body_force

Body force f (length-2 vector or function(x, y) returning a two-column matrix).

bcs

List of velocity_bc() and traction_bc() conditions.

value

Velocity c(ux, uy) or function(x, y) returning a two-column matrix.

marker

Boundary markers.

components

Velocity components to prescribe.

Value

An object of class stokes_problem. Its solution has components velocity (a vector solution with ux and uy, usable with errornorm()), pressure (an fe_function()) and diagnostics (including the L2 norm of div u_h).

Details

-div(nu grad u) + grad p = f, div u = 0

for velocity u and pressure p, discretized with the inf-sup stable Taylor-Hood pair: continuous P2 velocity and P1 pressure. Velocity conditions are given with velocity_bc() (any components, data may vary in space); traction_bc() prescribes the pseudo-traction (nu grad u - p I) n, and boundary parts with no condition get the do-nothing outflow condition (zero pseudo-traction). When the velocity is prescribed on the whole boundary, the pressure is fixed by a zero-mean gauge.

solve_pde() solves the saddle-point system by sparse LU (method = "lu", the default) or by right-preconditioned GMRES with the block-diagonal preconditioner diag(A, M_p / nu) (method = "gmres"), where A is the velocity Laplacian (factorized once) and M_p the pressure mass matrix; its iteration count does not grow with mesh refinement.

References

Taylor, C. and Hood, P. (1973). A numerical solution of the Navier-Stokes equations using the finite element technique. Computers and Fluids, 1, 73-100. Elman, H., Silvester, D. and Wathen, A. (2014). Finite Elements and Fast Iterative Solvers, 2nd edition. Oxford University Press.

Examples

# Lid-driven cavity
m <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 8)
p <- stokes_problem(m, bcs = list(velocity_bc(c(0, 0)), velocity_bc(c(1, 0), "top")))
s <- solve_pde(p)
range(s$velocity$ux$values)
#> [1] -0.1789024  1.0000000
